svg.title: Factoring a coefficient equation preserves the zero solution
svg.desc: In one plus a x to the fifth power, the coefficients of x and x squared are five a and ten a squared. Equating them and factoring gives five a times two a minus one equals zero. This yields a equals zero or one half. Both satisfy the original coefficient equation. Dividing by a before checking zero would lose a valid solution. Reject zero only if the question excludes it.
